blocks.text: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — Fourteen of the country’s 22 active petroleum service contracts (PSCs) are located in waters surrounding Palawan, raising concerns over potential threats to marine biodiversity, protected areas and coastal communities, an environmental group said. The Center for Energy, Ecology, and Development (CEED) raised the alarm on Friday in its report, “Don’t Drill Paradise,” a scoping paper on oil and gas exploration and development in the Philippines. The report said at least four of the 14 contract areas in Palawan were near protected areas, including the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park, the El Nido-Taytay Managed Resource […]...
